title: Living Things and What They Need

questions.stem: Which one is a living thing?
questions.explanation: A goat is alive. It eats, grows and has young. A stone, a bicycle and a chair are never alive.

questions.stem: Sort the pictures into living and non-living.
questions.explanation: Worms, flowers and goats grow, feed and have young, so they are living. A teddy bear, a bicycle and a stone are non-living.

questions.stem: Living things need food, air and ___ to stay alive.
questions.explanation: All living things need water. Food, water and air keep them alive.

questions.stem: A mango tree is not alive because it cannot walk.
questions.explanation: A mango tree is alive. It grows, takes in water through its roots and makes seeds. Plants do not need to walk to be alive.

questions.stem: A toy car is alive because it moves.
questions.explanation: A car can move, but it cannot grow, feed or have young. Things that only move are not alive.

questions.stem: What do living things do? Choose all that are right.
questions.explanation: Living things grow, have young and need food. Wheels and batteries belong to machines, not to living things.

questions.stem: Match each picture to what a living thing needs.
questions.explanation: Living things need food, water, light and warmth, and a safe place to live (shelter).

questions.stem: Living things grow and change. Put these pictures in order from youngest to oldest.
questions.explanation: A person starts as a baby, grows into a child, then an adult, and later becomes an older person.

questions.stem: Which thing do all living things do?
questions.explanation: All living things grow. Not all of them talk or fly.

questions.stem: Raju's toy robot can move and make sounds. Is it alive?
options: No. It cannot grow, eat or have young.
questions.explanation: A robot can move and make sounds, but it does not grow, eat or have young. So it is not alive.

questions.stem: Sort these. Which ones do living things need?
questions.explanation: Living things need food, water, air and shelter to stay alive. They can live without toys, sweets or a television.

questions.stem: Class 1 watered one plate of bean seeds. They kept another plate dry. After one week, 9 seeds grew on the wet plate and ___ seeds grew on the dry plate.
questions.explanation: No seeds grew on the dry plate. The seeds needed water to start growing.

questions.stem: Arif finds a stone by the river. It rolled down the hill, so he thinks it is alive. Which question helps him most?
questions.explanation: Living things eat and grow. A stone has no food, never grows and cannot have babies. Water pushed it, so it only moved.

questions.stem: Sumi forgot to give her pot plant ___ for a week. Its leaves are drooping.
questions.explanation: Plants need water. Without it the leaves droop. Sumi should water her plant.

questions.stem: Imran keeps a pet goat. What must he give it? Choose all that are right.
questions.explanation: A goat needs food, water and a shelter to stay safe and warm. A toy car and a bicycle are things it does not need.

questions.stem: Joy has a small pot plant. Where should he put it so that it grows well?
questions.explanation: Plants need light and warmth to grow well. A sunny window sill gives them both.

questions.stem: Look at the four plants. What happens to a plant that has no water?
questions.image_alt: Four potted plants: one healthy, one wilted with no water, one pale with no light and one small because it is too cold.
questions.explanation: The plant with no water droops. The plant with no light turns pale. The plant that is too cold stays small.

questions.stem: Which pictures show living things? Choose all that are right.
questions.explanation: A cat, a butterfly and a rice plant are alive. They grow and need food. A chair and a bicycle are made by people and are never alive.

questions.stem: Look at the picture. A chick grows into a hen.
questions.image_alt: Life cycle of a chicken: egg, hatching, chick, adult hen.
questions.explanation: The picture shows an egg, then a chick, then an adult hen. Living things grow and change.

questions.stem: Mina tests if bean seeds need water. Which test is fair?
options: One plate wet on the window sill. One plate dry in a dark cupboard.
One plate wet on the window sill. One plate dry on the same window sill.
Both plates wet on the window sill.
questions.explanation: In a fair test only one thing changes. Both plates sit in the same place, and only the water is different. In the first test, the light changes too.

questions.stem: Look at this list: cat, chair, mango tree, stone, snail, bicycle. How many living things are in it?
questions.explanation: The cat, the mango tree and the snail are living. The chair, the stone and the bicycle are non-living. That makes 3.

questions.stem: Mina thinks a toy car is alive because it moves. Tell one thing a living thing does that a car cannot do.
questions.model_answer: A living thing can grow, eat or have young. A car cannot.
questions.explanation: Living things grow, eat, breathe and have young. A car cannot do any of these, so it is not alive.

questions.stem: Put the steps in order to grow a bean plant.
sequence: Plant a bean seed in soil.
The shoot grows into a bean plant.
questions.explanation: A seed needs water to start growing. First a shoot comes up, then it grows into a plant.

questions.stem: In the seed test, 9 seeds grew on the wet plate and 0 on the dry plate. What does the test show?
questions.explanation: Only the water was different between the plates, so the test shows that seeds need water. It did not test soil or music.
